Okay, everyone, come closer to the fire. When I was your age, my family used to come here every summer. We didn't have a van. We used to drive down in a tiny old car, with the boards on the top and the tent in the back. We used to sleep in a tent in the forest, and we cooked fish on a campfire every night. Back then it was a quiet town. Most people used to work on farms, and there weren't any cafes. My dad used to say, if you see three cars at the beach, it's crowded. Nowadays it's very different. There are cafes and wineries everywhere, and a lot of tourists in summer. And every year the best surfers in the world come here for a big contest. But the waves are the same. Big, cold and beautiful. Now, go to bed. Your first heat is tomorrow.

Can I tell you a secret, mate? When I was a grommet, I used to be scared of big waves. Really scared. On big days I used to sit on the sand and just watch. I used to surf with my older brother, on his old longboard, because I didn't have my own board. And I didn't use to eat breakfast before a heat. I used to feel sick. Nowadays it's different. I still don't eat a lot before a heat, but I stretch, I listen to music, and I feel ready. So if you've got butterflies tomorrow, that's normal. Everybody does. Okay. Good night.
